problem.problem:
Bob is blue. Bob is furry. Dave is white. Erin is green. Erin is white. Gary is green. Gary is red. If Erin is furry and Erin is blue then Erin is big. Red things are round. If something is blue and big then it is white. Red, furry things are white. If something is round then it is furry. If something is furry and green then it is blue. Blue, white things are furry. If something is green then it is red.

Determine whether the following statement is true, false, or unknown:
Gary is furry.

Predicates:
Blue($x, bool) ::: Is x blue?
Furry($x, bool) ::: Is x furry?
White($x, bool) ::: Is x white?
Green($x, bool) ::: Is x green?
Red($x, bool) ::: Is x red?
Big($x, bool) ::: Is x big?
Round($x, bool) ::: Is x round?

Facts:
Blue(Bob, True) ::: Bob is blue.
Furry(Bob, True) ::: Bob is furry.
White(Dave, True) ::: Dave is white.
Green(Erin, True) ::: Erin is green.
White(Erin, True) ::: Erin is white.
Green(Gary, True) ::: Gary is green.
Red(Gary, True) ::: Gary is red.

Rules:
Furry(Erin, True) && Blue(Erin, True) >>> Big(Erin, True) ::: If Erin is furry and Erin is blue then Erin is big.
Red($x, True) >>> Round($x, True) ::: Red things are round.
Blue($x, True) && Big($x, True) >>> White($x, True) ::: If something is blue and big then it is white.
Red($x, True) && Furry($x, True) >>> White($x, True) ::: Red, furry things are white.
Round($x, True) >>> Furry($x, True) ::: If something is round then it is furry.
Furry($x, True) && Green($x, True) >>> Blue($x, True) ::: If something is furry and green then it is blue.
Blue($x, True) && White($x, True) >>> Furry($x, True) ::: Blue, white things are furry.
Green($x, True) >>> Red($x, True) ::: If something is green then it is red.

Query:
Furry(Gary, True) ::: Gary is furry.
